payload.title: [native-swift-2] In-flight callCommand continuation leaks (hangs forever) when the socket drops after the frame ...
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-swift-2 (medium/resource-leak, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: packages/swift/Sources/FrickSwift/FrickSyncSocket.swift
LINES: 1140-1158, 1635-1667

WHAT: `callCommand` registers a `CheckedContinuation` in `pendingCallResponders[requestId]` and sends the frame via `sendOrQueue(expectResponse:false)`. When the socket is `.connected`, the frame is transmitted and dropped from the outbound buffer. If the WebSocket then drops before the matching `CallCommandResult`/`Nack` arrives, `handleDisconnect` (lines 1635-1667) tears down the task and reconnects but does NOT resume or remove `pendingCallResponders` (nor `pendingResponders`). On reconnect only `activeSubscriptions` and the `pending` outbound buffer are replayed — the already-sent call frame is not, so the server never re-processes it and never replies. The continuation is resumed only in `close()` (lines 985-988). There is no timeout. The same leak affects `upsertObject`'s `pendingResponders`.

IMPACT: `FrickCallSession.join()/accept()/leave()/end()/setMediaState()` (and any `upsertObject`) awaited across a mid-flight reconnect never returns: the call UI spinner/disabled button hangs indefinitely and the awaiting task leaks until the socket is explicitly `close()`d. Common on flaky mobile networks.

SUGGESTED FIX: In `handleDisconnect`, fail (or, for idempotent retriable ops, re-queue) all `pendingCallResponders`/`pendingResponders` with a reconnect/cancellation error, mirroring `close()`. Or add a per-request timeout that resumes-throwing and removes the responder.
